newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deputies back justice reform bill.
newsitem.headline: French deputies back justice reform bill.

text.p: French deputies on Wednesday approved a bill overhauling the assize court system for serious criminal cases and allowing appeals against verdicts for the first time since the 1789 French Revolution.
Parties of the centre-right ruling coalition, as well as opposition Socialists and Communists, voted in favour of the bill at the National Assembly (lower house).
Under the reform an initial verdict would be handed down by a court with five jurors and any appeal against that verdict would be heard by a court with nine jurors.

In another innovation, jurors would have to detail "the reasons for their judgment". Current provisions demand only that jurors examine their conscience. The minimum age for jurors would be brought down to 18 from 23 years old.
The bill has yet to be approved by the Senate (upper house).
